record_notes.DCP-LETT-3791: Saturday,supplied March7,1857 copy. Both blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Falconer read a manuscript paragraph aloud to Darwin; no written incoming letter or exact manuscript passage is preserved here. March4–7 London visit and March11 society reading support proposed day, distinct from later1857 publication. Darwin suggests hypothetical Owen reply restricting tooth-law to placentals, explicitly uncertain memory of scope and group name; neither established Owen response nor unconditional agreement. Later April21 announcement is editorial context, not already heard on March7. Published p276 probable correspondence is not exact manuscript proof.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2175: November23,1857 copy: three cover blocks, complete eight-question enclosure, four footnotes and bibliography read. Enclosure has separate signed November22 date. Oral Falconer offer to contact Dickey, then requested immediate dispatch, not actual response. Copyist reports January13 later routing to Buist, not a November delivery event. Horse questions preserve quoted Gwatkin report versus Darwin puzzles about pure mares, dun/grey stripe patterns, cream/chestnut variants, inheritance, cob build and foal changes; all enquiries not results. Nested published quotation from Smith1843 is not a current incoming letter. Later Variation mention cannot recover Dickey/Buist answers.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1848: April3,supplied1856 ALS; three blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Oral London promise of boulder note/sketch and iceberg observations, now requested with location, height, isolation and size. Additional written question sheet is mentioned;6520 preserves beauty questions but exact identification of the whole April3 enclosure is not proved and it lacks geological answers. P1 position,, duplicated comma and headings need source-aware cleanup later. No new Mantell delivery established by this reminder; later Natural selection use is a separate witness.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1663: April10,supplied1856 ALS; six blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Acknowledges substantive earlier reply about quartz blocks but remains doubtful of erratic versus in-situ identity and asks Harris clarification with still-awaited iceberg sketch. Hairy otter/beaver report queried, alternative bird/reptile proposed. P5 still fears Mantell cannot answer beauty question, so later6520 written Yes cannot safely be made its prompt. Later interleaved Mantell answers have their own uncertain date. Body obliged to for has possible missing word held for source-backed repair. Footnote3 says April3[1865] despite actual1856 relation, and summary cites1854letter1603 rather than immediate1848; apparatus discrepancies not silently converted into new chronology.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1892: June5 in four discrete alternative years1856/57/58/59, not a continuous single-day certainty. Five blocks, four notes and bibliography read. Iceberg particulars now received; thinks all previous questions fully answered but wording does not uniquely identify6520 answer sheet or fix its arrival. Barnacle specimen museum inspection is future, no proof already seen. Return to New Zealand future and rat/frog requests unanswered. Aboriginal rat wording retained as Darwin wording, contrasted only in excluded modern apparatus; later Origin explanation not inserted. Exact year/period held.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2206: January24,supplied1857 ALS; three blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Palliser North American expedition, not Austrian Novara expedition of other letters. Darwin disclaims regional expertise and offers carboniferous-plant collection and erratic-boulder extent as proposals, not findings. Admiralty Manual instructions already published; cited1849/1851 editions distinguish authored instructions from unlocated Sharpey enquiry. No incoming source survives in current pool.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2073F: April9,supplied1857 complete five-block four-page ALS despite F suffix. Thirteen notes and bibliography read. Marked library catalogue selections are acts already performed, particular lists not transcribed; domestic variation book importance prospective. Davidson/Sorby/Beckles/Smith recommendations versus expressly unexamined Smyth writing, future election dates not current results. Sabine letter to Lyell forwarded to Darwin is an explicit access route, but actual source missing. Darwin surprised by grant committee membership; later July grant approval does not date April letter knowledge. Separate committee note said written is unlocated, cannot be synthesized or substituted with another grant note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2093F: May22,supplied1857 complete seven-page ALS in four retained blocks despite F suffix. Six footnotes and bibliography read. Shares Huxley assessment of Hancock but not proof he read newly submitted manuscript; Royal Society May14 reading versus1858 printing distinct. Prefers Prestwich if no strong botanist, would seek Lyell judgment in counterfactual council membership; not actual Lyell endorsement. Sharpey missing letter leads inference Copley not natural sciences this year; actual1857Chevreul and1858Lyell awards future. P4 after signature is authorial counterfactual method for assessing influence, not editorial addition. Unusually strong Lyell claim is explicitly Darwin judgment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2100: June2,supplied1857 ALS. Three full blocks,five notes and bibliography read. Hooker reports Lindley nomination and council reading of previous private Sharpey letter; no surviving incoming Hooker wording located in current pool. Darwin now prefers Lindley over Hancock/Prestwich, justified by broad botanical reading though not botanist. This revises conditional earlier recommendation, not evidence prior letter already favored Lindley. Assumed private audience versus actual institutional circulation causes concern about dogmatic tone; not repudiation of convictions. Later1857/1858/1865 awards remain apparatus.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1958: September22,supplied1856 ALS. Four blocks,six notes and bibliography read. Queries Temminck rock-pigeon classification against Gosse bald-pate description and requests sound comparison; no demonstrated conclusion yet. Asks West Indian feral rabbit, canary and domestic pigeon bodies; Madeira spirit specimen already held is distinct from requested island specimens. May1856 and1852 book reading dates are earlier evidence, not current first access. No proof later requested specimens actually sent; modern negative publication note not a complete archival absence claim.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1962: September28,1856 ALS with erroneous1867 endorsement; four blocks,four notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing Gosse response sufficient on bald-pate, actual coo still to be heard. Intends write Richard Hill this post; no proven exact mailing/receipt solely from intention. P4 after closing seeks dispersal evidence, ongoing salt/earth/seed experiments and land-mollusc puzzle. Later Origin opercular conclusion not current knowledge. Missing Gosse letter cannot be replaced by either Darwin outgoing1958 or later Hill incoming.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2082: April27,supplied1857 Moor Park ALS. Seven blocks,eight notes and bibliography read. Actual freshwater hatchling experiment: adhesion to dried duck foot and survival10/12/15hours,a few24 in damp air. Nibbling hypothesis explicitly doubted; hypothetical heron transport and consequent distribution inference separate from direct adhesion/survival observations. Analogous marine-littoral experiment requested, not performed; later memoir claim Gosse sent ample notes does not supply exact prompt or results. Criticizes Forbes land-bridge reasoning without claiming all possible dispersal solved. Hill useful correspondent already obtained through Gosse. Crustacean battle enquiry after signature unanswered; later Horace translation belongs apparatus, authentic Latin stays source.
